page.layout: One page of text, with a woodcut initial at the start of the first paragraph. Running head at the top, a division heading "CONCIO XXIII", a scripture reference line beneath it, then one paragraph of italic text. No margin notes. Page number at the top right. Signature "L" at the foot.

p.i: Custodi fili mi praeceptum patris tui, & ne deseras legem matris tuae. Liga ea super cor tuum iugiter, & adnecte ea gutturi tuo. Cum ambulaveris ducet te, & cum dormieris custodiet te, & cum evigilaveris ipsa loquetur tecum. Quia lucerna est praeceptum, & lex est lumen: atq; via vitae, correptio & castigatio. Ut custodiat te a muliere mala, & a blanditiis linguae extraneae. Non concupiscas pulchritudinem eius in corde tuo, ne capiat te palpebris suis. Quoniam propter mulierem meretricem (peruenit fornicator) usque ad massam panis, & mulier venatur preciosam animam viri. Numquid fouebit aliquis ignem in sinu suo, ut vestimenta sua non comburantur? Aut si gradietur quis supra carbones ut pedes eius non aduruntur? Sic qui ingreditur ad uxorem proximi sui, non innoxius erit, quisquis accesserit ad eam. page.notes: The woodcut initial is a decorated C; joined to the first word as "Custodi". The first word is printed as "Vstodi" beside the woodcut. The page number "161" is partly worn and uncertain. The running head is set in decorative capitals. Proverbs 6:20-22 is printed in the text with the printed spellings, including "adnecte", "deseras" (long s, possibly with an abbreviation mark), and "septu-" at the line end, which continues on the next page. The "L" at the foot is a gathering signature.
